title: Separate intervals under inverse image, Tate tensor and shift
statement: Fix a characteristic-p field k, primes ell!=p, a finite extension E/Q_ell and the specified geometric operations on ordinary strict varying-coefficient towers [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Use the bounds, twist and normalized Tate data of [def-sp-chart-tate-tower-data]. (i) For any k-morphism X->Y of Noetherian k-schemes, the specified ordinary derived inverse image preserves intrinsic finite-Tor constructibility at every level and any two prescribed cohomological and Tor intervals [a,b], [s,t]. (ii) On any Noetherian k-scheme T, tensor with the degree-zero strict Tate tower of any nonnegative exponent r, with the specified finite lines and quotient transitions, preserves those same bounds. (iii) For any scheme T and any integer j, shifting an actual tower by j changes these four endpoints to a-j,b-j,s-j,t-j. No normalization of the input tower is assumed.

proof.text: At a fixed level put $R=A_n$. The finite twist of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed] is $\mathbf Z_\ell(1)\otimes_{\mathbf Z_\ell}R$, by ordinary tensor associativity. With $B=R$ and $r=n$, [lem-amb-root-tower-finite-tensor] identifies it with $\mu_{\ell^n}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^n}R$ on the pro-etale site. This is the comparison pullback of the small-etale twist: indeed, on an etale cover trivializing $\mu_{\ell^n}$, choose its generator $\zeta$; on both sites $a\mapsto\zeta^a$ identifies the root sheaf with the constant $\mathbf Z/\ell^n$ sheaf. The comparison is therefore an isomorphism locally and hence globally. Such etale covers exist by [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line] with $A=\mathbf Z/\ell^n$, and tensor commutes with pullback by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-module-pullback-tensor]. By [lem-asd-finite-etale-twist-line], its $c$th tensor power is etale locally $R$ for every $c\ge0$, including $c=0$. Tensor by this line is exact, and thus its ordinary and derived tensors agree. The prime $\ell$ is invertible on all schemes in question because $\ell\ne p$.

source.place: Local pairs and Uniformity: finite Tate-line identification

proof.text: Choose the witness $L_n$ for $K_n$ from Step 2 with cohomological interval $[a,b]$ and Tor interval $[u,v]$. Apply [lem-sp-etale-scalar-flat-model] with the identity map $R\to R$ to obtain a flat constructible representative $P_n$ supported in $[u,v]$. For $g=p_de:U\to Y$, [lem-sp-etale-pullback-line-flat-model] applied to $P_n$, the finite twist line $R_U(d)$ of Step 4 and shift $2d$ proves that $(g^*L_n)(d)[2d]$ is constructible and has Tor interval $[u-2d,v-2d]$. Its cohomological interval is the sharper $[a-2d,b-2d]$: inverse image is exact by [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact], exact functors commute with cohomology by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], and tensor by the flat constructible line preserves $[a,b]$ by [lem-fd-flat-constructible-tensor]. Finally $H^i(C[2d])=H^{i+2d}(C)$. The pullback comparison [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback] identifies the pro-etale image of this witness with $e^*p_d^*K_n(d)[2d]$. Its Tor interval passes to the pro-etale site by [det-pe-finite-tor-comparison-noetherian]; its cohomological interval and intrinsic constructibility pass by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-ring-constructible-derived-origin]. Tensor comparison can be computed on $P_n$: comparison pullback preserves its flat terms by [lem-pe-constructible-comparison-flat-pullback], so the ordinary monoidal comparison of Step 4 computes the derived comparison as well.

proof.text: Termwise inverse image gives an actual strict tower functor: the quotient-linear transition maps are pulled back with their scalar actions. It is exact, since its components are exact by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-exact] and tower kernels and cokernels are componentwise by [det-sp-coefficient-towers-abelian]. Likewise termwise tensor by the specified Tate-line tower is exact, since each component line of Step 4 is locally free of rank one; its transitions are the prescribed quotient transitions. Thus these operations descend to the ordinary derived tower category and evaluate to the finite operations, as also specified in [det-sp-tower-shriek-levels]. Apply Step 5 at each stage. After $r$ of the $d$ ordered affine-line pullback/twist/shift operations, the common intervals are $[a-2r,b-2r]$ and $[u-2r,v-2r]$: the base $r=0$ is $K$, and one further operation preserves the endpoints under pullback and twist and subtracts $2$ under $[2]$. The final etale pullback preserves both intervals. Partial stages before a twist or shift follow by the same formulas. Hence $H_UK$ and every intermediate object belong to the indicated uniform subcategory, with bounded-below actual towers by Step 3 and separate etale-origin-level witnesses by Step 2.

proof.text: Apply the finite-ring constructible derived origin theorem and specified Tor-interval comparison separately to every level. Transport the finite inverse image and flat-line tensor through the normalized evaluation comparisons; shift homology reindexes all endpoints.

lean.statement:
theorem elementary_tower_bounds
    (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (k : Type u) [Field k] [CharP k p] (hlp : l ≠ p)
    (base : SpTowerShriek.Base l E) (ops : SpTowerShriek.Operations l E base) :
    (∀ (X Y : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsNoetherian X.left] [IsNoetherian Y.left]
      (f : X ⟶ Y) (C : SpTowerShriek.D l E Y.left) (a b s t : ℤ),
      bounds l E Y.left C a b s t →
      bounds l E X.left ((SpTowerShriek.pull l E base (ops.geometry f.left)).obj C)
        a b s t) ∧
    (∀ (T : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsNoetherian T.left] (w : Twists l E T.left)
      (C : SpTowerShriek.D l E T.left) (r : ℕ) (a b s t : ℤ),
      bounds l E T.left C a b s t →
      bounds l E T.left (twist l E base w C r) a b s t) ∧
    (∀ (T : Scheme.{u}) (C : SpTowerShriek.D l E T) (j a b s t : ℤ),
      bounds l E T C a b s t →
      bounds l E T (C⟦j⟧) (a - j) (b - j) (s - j) (t - j))
